data.summary:
Units are placed on the battlefield before they can move or attack, most often at deployment but sometimes for other reasons. When a rule calls for setting up a unit, its models must be placed with:

- the unit in coherency (03.03)
- the unit unengaged (03.04)
- every other requirement and restriction met

If any model cannot be placed, remove the unit and return it to where it came from, such as strategic reserves or inside a **TRANSPORT**. If this happens during a move type, the unit counts as never selected to move, so it can be selected later to try again or to remain stationary (09.04).

A model too large to meet its set-up restrictions is placed by the case that applies:

- At deployment: if its base cannot fit wholly in your deployment zone, place it touching your battlefield edge.
- From strategic reserves: if its base cannot fit within the required distance of the edge, place it touching any battlefield edge.
- Disembarking: units normally go wholly within 3" of their **TRANSPORT**; a model too big for that (typically over 3" across in every direction) goes with its base no more than 1" from the hull or base of the **TRANSPORT**, unengaged.

In the turn such a model arrives at deployment or from strategic reserves, its unit cannot make normal, advance, fall-back or charge moves or any ranged attacks; **AIRCRAFT** models arriving from strategic reserves are exempt. Models such as **AIRCRAFT** whose parts extend well past their base may overhang the deployment zone (base still wholly inside) or a battlefield edge (still more than 8" from every enemy unit) when nothing else works.

To redeploy, remove the unit and deploy it again under the normal rules, for example with Infiltrators if all its models have it.
